parties:
M M Rahman ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Chairman, RAJUK and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: In this Rule respondents were called upon to show cause as to why the auction notice published in the newspaper the Daily Star, on the 31st day of May, 1995 inviting applications by the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha from the intending bidders for auction sale of plot No.10 (Old 16-17) of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and of no legal effect and as to why they should not be directed to issue letter of allotment in favour of the petitioner in respect of the said plot and complete all the formalities in executing and registering the lease deed thereof or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, in short, are that, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha, hereinafter referred to as the RAJUK, published notice in the newspaper the Daily Ittefaq, on 2-7-1985 for auction sale of commercial plot No. 10 (Old 16-17) measuring an area more or less 9.5 kathas in Gulshan North Commercial Area; that petitioner submitted tender attaching Pay Order dated 15-7-1985 for an amount of Taka 50,000.00 issued by the Janata Bank towards security money, that petitioner purchased the tender documents in his name, that petitioner''s offer for per katha of land at an amount of Taka 5,52,000.00 being the highest, the same was accepted by the RAJUK; that after accepting the bid petitioner was asked by the RAJUK that in due course letter of allotment would be issued; that upon acceptance of petitioner''s offer RAJUK encased and adjusted the money that was deposited as security money towards the amount that was to be paid as the first installment; that the adjustment was made in terms and conditions of the tender document; that by adjustment of security money towards the amount due as against first installment the petitioner was recognized as the successful bidder and purchaser of the land of plot No. 10 (Old 16-17) of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka; that issuances of allotment letter having been delayed petitioner wrote on different occasions to the RAJUK to issue the letter of allotment, but every time he was assured that it would be issued, that on 31st May, 1995 petitioner to his utter surprise and to his great shock noticed notification in the newspaper the Daily Star, dated 31st May, 1995 published by the RAJUK inviting offer from the intending bidders for sale of plot No. 10 of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka; that having had seen notice in the daily newspaper petitioner tried to meet respondent No.1 and to ascertain the reason for publishing the notice for auction of the land that has already been sold in auction to the petitioner; that petitioner could not meet them as the respondents did not give him any interview. In the foretasted facts and circumstances petitioner moved this court calling in question legality of auction of the respondents in publishing notice inviting offer for selling the plot No.10 of Gulshan North Commercial Area in auction and has obtained the Rule.

3. It is the contention of the petitioner that auction that was held in pursuance to the advertisement made in the newspaper on 2-7-1985 and that in the said auction petitioner''s bid having been accepted and that thereby he having had acquired an interest in the land of plot No.10 of Gulshan North Commercial Area the action of respondents, particularly respondent Nos.1-3, in publishing notice signifying intention to sell the land plot No. 10 of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka again through public action is illegal, that petitioner''s bid having been accepted by adjustment of security money and that he having been assured by the respondents of issuance of letter of allotment and that in disregard of the same respondent Nos.1-3 having had published notice to sell the land that was already sold to the petitioner the respondents acted illegally and without jurisdiction; that auction of the respondent Nos.1-3 by way of publishing notice in the newspaper the Daily Star, on 31-5-1995 for sale of the land in question was made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect; that action of respondents are arbitrary, malafide, unjust, whimsical, capricious and violative of the principle of natural justice, that respondents 1-3 are under legal obligation to issue letter of allotment in respect of the land in question in favour of the petitioner since they have accepted the petitioner''s bid by way of adjustment of security money and that bid so accepted having not been cancelled.

4. Respondent Nos. 1-3 have entered appearance and have filed affidavit-in-opposition denying the material averments made in the writ petition. Their case, in short, is that, it is not correct to say that tender form was purchased by the petitioner MM Rahman and that security money was deposited by the petitioner; that tender form was purchased by KT Corporation Limited of 60, Gulshan Avenue and the said KT Corporation was represented by one MM Rahman; that in the auction held on 17-7-1985 in respect of the plot No.10 of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka KT Corporation Limited was the highest bidder by offering Taka 5,52,000.00 per katha; that MM Rahman participated in the bid on behalf of KT Corporation Limited; that KT Corporation''s bid being the highest the same was accepted and that provisional letter of allotment was issued on 5-8-1985 in the name of KT Corporation Limited; that provisional letter of allotment was sent to the KT Corporation Limited through the messenger; that provisional letter of allotment was entered in the issue register and the same was sent to the KT Corporation Limited at its address at 60, Gulshan Avenue South; that the letter was received by a representative of the addressee; that after issuance of provisional letter of allotment security money that was deposited by the KT Corporation as a pre-condition of participation in the auction was adjusted; that petitioner''s claim of being highest bidder is not true; that it is the KT Corporation Limited that was the highest bidder in the auction and that said KT Corporation was represented by MM Rahman; that petitioner MM Rahman participated in the bid as representative of KT Corporation and not in his individual capacity or in his individual identity; that respondents accepted the bid of the KT Corporation Limited and not of the petitioner since in the auction held petitioner had no separate entity or identity other than being a representative of the KT Corporation; that papers annexed in the writ petition, particularly the bid sheet, were not genuine, but the same are fabricated papers brought into existence for the purpose of the writ petition, that petitioner''s contention of giving assurance by the respondents as to issuance of letter of allotment is not true since there was no occasion to give such assurance by the respondents to the petitioner as he was not a bidder in the auction; that the respondents adjusted the security money that was deposited by KT Corporation Limited as the said organization was the highest bidder and that security money so adjusted was not of the petitioner, that petitioner''s claim of assuring him as to issuance of letter of allotment is frivolous statement in that provisional letter of allotment was issued in August, 1985 to the KT Corporation, the highest bidder in the auction and that KT Corporation to whom letter of allotment was issued having not deposited the amount of installment security money stood forfeited and that KT Corporation''s inchoate right stood extinguished; that letters annexed to the writ petition said to have been written by the petitioner requesting the RAJUK to issue letter of allotment are not genuine, that KT Corporation Limited having not deposited the amount towards installment within the time specified in the provisional letter of allotment the provisional letter of allotment stood cancelled; that auction notice as was published on 31st May, 1995 in the Daily Star was legally published since the bid made by the KT Corporation Limited in the auction held on 17-7-1985 stood cancelled for his failure to deposit the 50% of the total price of the land and, as such, the notice so made was quite legal; that in making the publication of notice for auction of the plot no legal right of the petitioner has been infringed or violated since he was not the participant in the previous auction; that as the petitioner was not a bidder or, in other words, as he was not the participant in the auction that was held on 17-7-85 his contention of depriving him of his legal right of having letter of allotment in respect of the plot in question and that of having a document executed and registered in his favour by the respondents merits no consideration and, as such, he has no right to take exception or to challenge the legality of the notice so published in the newspaper the Daily Star on 31-5-1995; that the auction notice so published is quite genuine and not violative or contrary to the provision of law.

5. Petitioner has filed Affidavit-in-Reply to the Affidavit-in-Opposition of the respondents upon denying the material averments made therein and reiterating the statements made in the writ petition. In the reply it has also been asserted that the petitioner in his individual capacity and identity was the participant in the auction held on 17-7-1985 and that KT Corporation was nobody; that KT Corporation Limited has been inserted in the papers filed by the respondents to frustrate the legal claim of the petitioner in the plot in question and that also with a motive which is not bonafide; that tender form was purchased by the petitioner and that security money was deposited by him and that petitioner himself in his personal capacity and identity participated in the auction as evidenced by the bid sheet Annexure C to the petition; that petitioner being the highest bidder it was he who alone was entitled to get provisional letter of allotment; that petitioner being the highest bidder and that the same having been accepted and having not been cancelled, as such, respondents were under legal obligation to issue letter of allotment to him and him alone; that issuance of provisional letter of allotment to a fictitious person or to a firm that did not participate in the auction had in no way affected the petitioner''s right to having the letter of allotment; that respondents'' contention of forfeiting the security money for not depositing half of the price as was offered is not legally tenable in law in that no provisional letter of allotment was issued in the name of the petitioner who participated in the auction held on 17-7-1985 and was the highest bidder and the same was also accepted by the respondents.

6. Learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that petitioner being the successful bidder in the auction held on 17-7-1985 for sale of plot No.10 (Old 16-17) of Gulshan North Commercial Area, hereinafter referred to as the Commercial Plot, and that security money that he deposited having been adjusted against the price of the commercial plot the respondents were and are under legal obligation to issue letter of allotment and that to execute and register the necessary document and to make over possession of the land to him; that respondents'' contention of petitioner''s participation in the auction as representative of KT Corporation is nothing but figment of imagination in that it is the petitioner alone who participated in his own capacity in the auction and made the bid and that said fact is evidenced by the papers on the record, namely, Annexure B, B-1 and C; that the petitioner being the highest bidder and his bid having been accepted and till today having not been cancelled and that he being ready to deposit the money towards the price of the commercial plot the respondents acted illegally in not issuing the letter of allotment and that in denial of the petitioner''s legal right of having the letter of allotment in publishing notice for the auction of the commercial plot that has already been sold to the petitioner.

7. Learned Advocate appearing for the respondents submits that the writ petition so filed is not maintainable in that for enforcement of contractual obligation petitioner has sought for a direction upon invoking extraordinary constitutional jurisdiction, that petitioner having no legal right in the matter as regards which he has sought for direction from this court the reliefs sought in the writ petition are not available to him; that there having been no communication from the side of respondents signifying acceptance of petitioner''s bid and that it being within the absolute discretion of the respondents to accept or to reject the bid made in the auction held on 17-7-1985 petitioner in law also is not entitled to seek a direction from this court for the exercise of the said discretion in favour of the petitioner; that facts stated in the writ petition being highly disputed and contentious, as such, adjudication thereof as can only be made after extensive investigation or upon collection of evidence in a regular trial, this court in its summary jurisdiction is not competent in law to adjudicate such matters the Rule so obtained is liable to be discharged.

8. In support of the petitioner''s claim that he in his personal capacity and that not on behalf of anybody or that as representative of KT Corporation Limited, participated in the auction that was held on 17-7-1985 for selling the commercial plot being plot No.10 (Old 16-17) of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka he has annexed papers is Annexure B-Photo copy of the application filed expressing desire to participate in the auction and that photo copy of the tender paper containing terms and conditions, Annexure B-1, counterfoil of the Pay Order showing deposit of security money of Taka 50,000.00 and Annexure C-photo copy of the bid sheet. The respondents in their Affidavit disputed the genuineness of the papers, including bid sheet, filed by the petitioner in support of the claim of his being one of successful bidders and to have the provisional letter of allotment. The respondents except making a statement that the papers so filed by the petitioner in support of his claim that it is he who submitted tender papers in his name and that it is he who in his personal capacity and with individual identity participated in the bid, have not filed the papers is application filed by the petitioner expressing intention to participate in the auction and other related papers as were received by the respondents from the petitioner nor have produced the file before the court though we asked the learned Advocate for the respondents to ask his client to produce the record before the court and that on our query although the learned Advocate submitted that he communicated to his client to be present in court with the records and that his client communicated to him that in due course the record would be produced in court, but ultimately, the respondents had neither made over the records to their learned Advocate nor produced the same in court for ascertainment of the correctness or otherwise of the statement of the respondents in their Affidavit-in-opposition that tender papers were filed by the petitioner as representative of the KT Corporation Limited and that the petitioner participated in the auction as representative of the KT Corporation. To substantiate their averments made in the Affidavit-in-opposition petitioner MM Rahman participated in the auction held on 17-7-1985 on behalf of KT Corporation they (respondents) have annexed Annexure 1 (Photo copy of the register wherein particulars of pay order deposited towards security money were entered). Learned Advocate for the respondents at the time of making submission that petitioner MM Rahman participated in the auction and made the bid on behalf of KT Corporation Limited referred to the entry at serial No. 13 of Annexure-1 and submitted that photo copy of the register submitted in court is Annexure 1 correctly represents the contents of the register and thereupon placed the Register before the court. On looking at the entry in the Register it appears to us that below the writing MM Rahman the writings "for KT Corporation Ltd." has been written at a later stage by different hand and ink for certain purpose and motive which appears to be anything other than bonafide. So whatever credence could have been given to the Annexure I in connection with the submission that petitioner participated in the auction on behalf of KT Corporation Ltd but as it is seen from the Register that the writings "for KT Corporation Ltd." has been inserted in the Register by a different hand with different ink as seen from the ink used in the other entries including the writing MM Rahman the same has totally been vanished. The respondents, in support of their contention that the papers on the basis of which petitioner MM Rahman claiming himself to be a successful bidder and that the bid made by him in the auction held on 17-7-1985 in respect of the commercial plot was accepted are not genuine, have not laid any foundation therefor by producing the original papers namely, application made expressing intention to participate in the auction and the tender documents as well as bid sheet (Annexures B and C) which were in their possession. The respondents in their endeavor to raise the plea of disputed question (s) of fact have annexed bid sheet of plot No.41 at Chashara, Narayangonj as Annexure I instead of annexing bid sheet of Plot No.10 Gulshan North Commercial Area is plot in question nor has produced the said bid sheet before the court at the time of hearing. This attitude of the respondents manifests absence of bonafide on their part in the matter of not producing the relevant material paper (s). Since in the background of the facts as stated hereinbefore, in our opinion, respondents'' contention that KT Corporation Limited participated in the bid appears to be not genuine, rather the respondents have resorted to fabrication of papers to add force to their incorrect and untrue claim of KT Corporation Ltd''s participation in the bid, as such, we are of the view that petitioner''s claim of his participation in the auction held on 17-7-1985 and making bid and that acceptance thereof as evidenced by Annexure C to the writ petition is genuine and that it is he who participated in his individual capacity and in his right and that he did not represent anybody else as claimed by the respondents.

9. It is the contention of the petitioner that in spite of his asking for the issuance of the letter of allotment for the commercial plot and that in spite of assurances given by the respondents that in due course provisional letter of allotment would be issued, but the respondents without issuing the same to the petitioner published notice for the auction of the commercial plot ie. Plot No.10, which was earlier auctioned, and that the petitioner being the successful bidder his bid was accepted. In rebuttal of said contention of the petitioner, respondents contended that it was the KT Corporation Limited that participated in the auction and that provisional letter of allotment (Annexure II in the Affidavit-in-opposition) was issued to the said KT Corporation Ltd. with direction therein to deposit 50% of the total price of the land within the Specified time. The provisional letter of allotment that was said to have been issued to the KT Corporation Ltd is Annexure II in the Affidavit-in-Opposition. Since we have already taken the view that it is petitioner who participated in the auction held on 17-7-1985 and that the petitioner participated in the auction in the individual right and not representing anybody else as such, it appears that the provisional letter of allotment that is said to have been issued in the name of KT Corporation Ltd has been brought into existence for some ulterior purpose keeping which in mind in the Register maintained as regards the particulars of the intending participants in the auction and that also as regards the particulars of Pay Order deposited towards security money by the intending participants in the auction held in respect of the commercial plot in question KT Corporation Ltd''s name was inserted below the petitioner''s name. Since provisional letter of allotment was not issued in the name of the petitioner who participated in the auction and whose bid was accepted being the highest, but the same was issued in the name of an organization which was never the participant in the auction it cannot be said that failure on the part of fictitious organization, as claimed by the respondents to have participated in the auction or, in other words, failure on the part of the non-participant organization, in whose name the respondents were said to have issued the provisional letter of allotment and shown to have been received by the said organization, to deposit the money within the time stipulated in the provisional letter of allotment the bid of the petitioner that was accepted and that no letter of allotment was issued in the name of the petitioner asking him to deposit the half of the price within the specified time cannot be said or considered to have stood cancelled. It may be mentioned here that the fact of adjustment of the money that was deposited as security for participation in the auction is not disputed. But it is contended on behalf of the respondents that the security money has been forfeited since in the light of the provisional letter of allotment fifty percent of the price money was not deposited. As we have hereinbefore held that it cannot be said that petitioner''s bid that was accepted by the respondent stood cancelled or that there was any fault on the part of the petitioner in making deposit of the price of the commercial plot for which his bid could be cancelled, in our opinion, the bid so made by the petitioner and accepted by the respondents has remained valid, the notification that was made in the newspaper- The Daily Star on 31-5-1995 was not legal, and that since petitioner''s offer stands valid, having been accepted by the respondents, they are under legal obligation being statutory body to issue letter of allotment to the petitioner.

<u>10. On behalf of respondents it has been submitted that averments made in support of the reliefs sought in the writ petition having been denied and consequent thereupon the entire matter as has become highly contentious or, in other words, facts alleged in support of the reliefs sought in the writ petition having been denied by the respondents and thereupon as the matter involves resolution of disputed questions of fact as such, as this court in view of long series of decisions in its summary jurisdiction will not embark upon investigation or adjudicate upon the disputed questions of fact and consequent thereupon as the writ petition so filed is not maintainable the Rule is liable to be discharged. The submission so made apparently appears to be quite attracted in view of the settled principle of law that disputed questions of fact adjudication or resolution whereof requires elaborate or complicated investigation will not be gone into in writ jurisdiction where the nature of the proceeding is summary one and primarily decided on the statements made on affidavits by the parties and the documents annexed to the petition and the affidavit-in-opposition. But at the same time it is also settled principle of law that mere denying or disputing of the statements made in the petition and document annexed to the petition by the respondent does not render that fact a disputed fact when in support of denial no foundation has been laid by producing materials which could have been produced by the party who is denying or disputing the averments made and the documents annexed to the petition or, in other words, though contention has been made disputing the correctness of the facts averted by the petitioner but in support of such denial no material has been placed on record that will not take the matter, for the adjudication of which writ jurisdiction has been invoked, out of the court. Learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of his contention that mere disputing the petitioner''s contention does not take the matter, for the adjudication of which he has invoked the writ jurisdiction, out of jurisdiction of the court has referred to the case reported in 42 DLR (AD) 126 and 19 DLR (SC)</u>

11. In the instant case the respondents in support of their contention that petitioner MM Rahman was not the participant in the auction but KT Corporation Ltd. was the participant in the auction that was held on 17-7-1985 in connection with the sale of the commercial plot is plot No.10 of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka has not filed any paper to disclose the correctness of the fact as evidenced by Annexures B and C to the writ petition, rather the respondents have withheld the papers and filed papers which we have already found not genuine.

<u>12. On behalf of the petitioner learned Advocate has submitted that after acceptance of the bid a right has been created in petitioner''s favour, although not complete one but an inchoate one, still then at that stage or in that state of the matter he can very much invoke the writ jurisdiction seeking direction on the respondents to do what they are required to do in law and that not to do which they are not authorized in law to do. Direction under Article 102(2) of the Constitution can very much be sought and can be given against the person performing any function in connection with the affairs of the Republic or of a local authority in respect of an inchoate right in case of performance of any action by the specified authority, which the said authority in law is required to do, but that non action of the authority or non-performance of the duty required by the law to be performed without just cause or valid reason has made the right legally accrued inchoate turns or makes the inchoate right an established right or, in other words, a perfect right. Learned Advocate for the petitioner in support of the contention that action of the respondents is not immune from examination or scrutiny of the High Court Division under Article 102(2) of the Constitution on their mere contention that the matter as to which direction has been sought from this court is a contractual matter or that the action as to which direction has been sought relates to an act performed by respondents in contractual matter, has referred to the decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 293, 40 DLR (AD) 62, 37 DLR (AD) 117 and 7 BLD (AD) 106 (39 DLR (AD) 85).</u>

<u>13. From respondents'' side submission has been made that relief sought by the petitioner is not available to him since he is guilty of serious laches, in that auction was held on 17-7-1985 and the petitioner has filed the writ petition in 1995 seeking enforcement of the bid made in the bid auction that as claimed by the petitioner to have been accepted, in 1985. Petitioner has offered explanation, supported by the papers annexed to the writ petition (Annexure E Series), in the background of which he has not come earlier: seeking direction for the performance of the act that the respondents were required to do after the acceptance of the bid and that has stated the facts in the background of which he had no other alternative but to file the writ petition. The explanation so offered appears to us sufficient and reasonable and, as such, it cannot be said that petitioner is guilty of laches or petitioner has come before this court after an inordinate delay seeking direction against the respondents to do an act what they are required to do in law after the bid of the petitioner was accepted.</u>

<u>14. It has been submitted on behalf of the respondents that it was the total discretion of the respondents either to accept or to reject a bid and that respondents having had rejected the bid of KT Corporation, which is not correct in that, in fact, bid was made by the petitioner MM Rahman and that the bid of the petitioner MM Rahman was accepted, as the KT Corporation Limited defaulted in depositing half of the bid money and that petitioner being nobody in the matter of the auction that was held on 17-7-1985 in connection with commercial plot he cannot seek any direction as against the respondents for the exercise of their discretion in favour of the petitioner. In the instant case as seen from the papers on record (Annexures B and C to the petition) that petitioner in his self capacity participated in the auction and that his bid was accepted by the respondents and that being the position direction as has been sought by the petitioner or that the relief as has been prayed for in the writ petition is not one as to exercise discretion as claimed to be vested in the respondents either to accept or to reject the bid. Learned advocate for the respondents has submitted that it is quite within the competency of the respondents to cancel certain bid/offer made in an auction if they feel that cancellation, if made and that fresh auction, if held, that would fetch more revenue or money, and in that situation if the authority cancels a bid or rejects an offer then the authority acts quite legally. In support of the submission so made the learned Advocate has referred to the case reported in 17 BLD (1997) 227; 43 DLR 281 and 45 DLR 134.</u>

15. In the instant case as seen from the materials on record that petitioner''s offer that was accepted has not been cancelled in anticipation of a more lucrative bid or offer, rather petitioner''s bid has been considered to have stood cancelled for not depositing half of the total price offered in the light of the provisional letter of allotment (Annexure II in the Affidavit-in-opposition) issued in the name of an organization which, in fact, did not at all participate in the auction and, as such, the contention so made by the respondents that petitioner''s bid was cancelled on the consideration that if fresh auction was held that would fetch more revenue or money to the authority appears to be not correct.

<u>16. The other contention of the learned Advocate for the respondents is that in the absence of a right in-existence writ petition if any filed was not maintainable and in support of the said contention he has referred to the cases reported in 1952 SCR 28, AIR 1966 (SC) 334; AIR 1964 (SC) 685; 11 DLR (SC) 260 and 44 DLR 144.</u>

17. We have already held that petitioner''s bid was accepted by the authority and consequent thereupon he acquired a right to have the land allotted to him and that respondents were under legal obligation to issue letter of allotment to the petitioner asking him to deposit the price offered by him and in case of payment of the said amount to execute the necessary papers vesting the property in the petitioner but the respondents, for no fault of the petitioner, did not perform their said duty.

<u>18. The other contention of the respondents that contractual matters are beyond the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division and that contractual matters cannot be the subject matter for adjudication in a writ court appears to us not an absolute proposition, rather it is now well settled that when certain statutory body performs certain act/duty as part of their statutory function (s) and that in the performance of the said function (s) matters dealt with, even if are contractual in nature and that as regards the said matters if duties or statutory functions are not performed in accordance with law or in strict observance of legal formality or in case of inaction of the authority as the matter (s) what it was required to do or perform in a given set of facts, as in the instant case the authority was required to issue letter of allotment in the name of the petitioner, in that case the same can very much be a matter for scrutiny by a constitutional court. In the instant case we have seen that the respondents were under legal obligation after acceptance of the bid of the petitioner to do their duties for vesting the property in favour of the petitioner in case of his offering of the bid money on receiving the letter of allotment and the other ancillary things, but instead thereof the respondents have resorted to a practice which we have already held that same was anything other than bonafide one, and that resort to the said practice by the statutory body is highly deprecatory. The respondents in their affidavit-in-opposition made deliberate attempts upon withholding relevant papers and in their place annexed non releavant papers to make the averments made by the petitioner in support of the relief sought disputed one.</u>

<u>19. It has been contended on behalf of the respondents that the participation in an auction does not create any right in favour of the participant and, as such, as against the cancellation of the tender that was filed by the petitioner in the auction that was held in respect of the commercial plot he has no legal right to make grievance. In support of the aforesaid submission learned Advocate for the respondents has referred to the cases reported in PLD 1956 (SC) (India) 53 and 45 DLR 143. Suffice it to say that the facts of the case before us are quite different from the facts of the cases referred to by the learned Advocate for the respondents and, as such, the principle enunciated in the said reported cases has no manner of application to the instant case.</u>

<u>20. Reliance as has been placed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner in the decisions reported in 32 DLR (AD) 223, 40 DLR (AD) 62 and 37 DLR (AD) 117 as regards one''s right to seek redress even in respect of inchoate right are not applicable to the instant case in that in the said reported decisions principle of law was enunciated in the background of the facts wherein remedy was sought under the provision of the Specific Relief Act and that the decisions were made in the cases decided by the court in its ordinary civil jurisdiction and, as such, principle enunciated in those cases are not applicable, nor can be relied upon in a case considered by the court in its writ jurisdiction. Petitioner has filed the writ petition seeking direction upon the respondents to do what they were required to do in law after acceptance of petitioner''s bid and that as respondents had/have no cogent reasonable, rational and plausible reason(s) of refraining, themselves from performing the said duty and, as such, the relief sought in the writ petition is quite available to the petitioner.</u>

21. In view of the discussions made above we are of the view that the Rule obtained by the petitioner has substance and accordingly, the same is made absolute without any order as to costs. Respondents'' action in publishing notice in the newspaper-the Daily Star on 31st May, 1995 to auction the commercial plot No.10 (old 16-17) of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka is declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

Respondents are directed to do as they are required to do in law since petitioner''s bid that was made in the auction held on 17-7-1985 for sale of the land of plot No.10(Old 16-17) of Gulshan North Commercial Area, Dhaka has been accepted and to take steps for vesting the property by way of leasing out the property in case of petitioner''s payment of bid money that was made in the auction held on 17-7-1985 in respect of the plot as mentioned above and to do the other ancillary matters relating to the vesting of the property in the petitioner by the respondents No.1-3 within 6 (six) months from the date of making application, attaching certified copy of the judgment by the petitioner.

End.

lawyer:
No one appears—For the Petitioner. 
Shamim Khaled Ahmed, Advocate—For Respondent No. 6.
parties:
Edruk Ltd  ----- Petitioner
vs
Secretary, Ministry of Industries ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This Rule Nisi has been issued on an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the respondents should not be directed to implement the recommendation made by the Sick Industries Rehabilitation Cell in its report dated 25-8-1992 (Annexure-D-3) and rehabilitate the petitioner's sick industry and set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna in Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 42 of 2000 (Annexure-I and I-1) and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Respondent No. 6, Janata Bank as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 42 of 2000 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna claiming an amount of Taka 20,89,28,042.00 against the defendant-petitioner. The defendant petitioner duly appeared and filed a written statement denying the claim all together. The learned Judge of Artha Rin Adalat, Pabna on consideration of the materials on record decreed the suit on contest against the defendant petitioner by the impugned Judgment and decree dated 9-8-2003 (decree signed on 13-812003).

3. No one appears on behalf of the petitioner to press the Rule.

4. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 6 Janata Bank, on the other hand, contested the Rule by filing affidavit-in-opposition. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed in the course of argument has taken us through the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition along with annexures as filed therewith and then argues with force that the writ petition is not maintainable against the Judgment and Decree of Artha Rin Adalat. The learned Advocate to fortify this branch of his argument has relied on the decisions namely the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD)6, 59 DLR (AD) 6.

5. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed, next argues that the so-called recommendation of a Cabinet Committee cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not law. The learned Advocate in support of this submission has relied on the decisions namely the decisions reported in 7 BLT(AD) 313 and 59 DLR 141.

6. We have perused the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and the relevant papers as annexed therewith and also considered the submissions made by the learned Advocates for the respondent No. 6. To appreciate the submission made by the learned Advocate with regard to the question of maintainability it requires us to decide the question of maintainability of the instant writ petition before entering into the merit of the writ petition.

7. We have studied the cited decisions namely the decisions reported in 46 DLR (AD) 191, 54 DLR (AD) 6, and 59 DLR (AD) 6. In those decisions, we find our Appellate Division clearly spelt out that since there being special provision for appeal in the Artha Rin Adalat Ain no application under Article 102 of the Constitution lies against the judgment and decree of the Artha Rin Adalat.

<u>8. In view of the above well settled principle of law as to the question of maintain-ability of the Writ Petition, we have no hesitation to hold that the petitioner has miserably failed to cross the first hurdle, inasmuch as Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 is a special law and special provision having been provided in Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 for preferring appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. In order to save the valuable public time since the petitioner could not cross the first hurdle, we do not think it wise to advert all the grounds of the writ petition.</u>

9. In the case of Professor Abdur Rahim Khan vs Ministry of Industries reported in 7 BLT (AD) 313 wherein it has been laid down:

"It is true that the High Court Division suffered from a misconception of fact that there was already an agreement/contract between the parties and a dispute has arisen over the terms and conditions thereof which was the subject-matter of the writ petition. In fact, petitioners came with the writ petition for a direction upon the respondents to finalise the agreement only on the basis of the recommendation of the Cabinet Committee as approved by the Prime Minister vide aforesaid Memo dated 8-5-94. The High Court Division's misconception was there but the misconceived nature of the petitioners' writ petition was equally showing. Unfortunately, the High Court Division failed to take notice of the same and proceeded upon a wrong ground of fact. The recommendation of a Cabinet Committee cannot be enforced through a writ for the simple reason that it is not law. It is as simple as that. The Writ Petition was misconceived at the inception."

<u>10. In view of the decision quoted above, we are led to hold that the contention of the petitioner with regard to implement the recommendation made by the Sick Industries Rehabilitation Cell in its report dated 25-8-1992 does not find any leg to stand upon or the same bears no binding force to the Court in any way.</u>

11. In view of the discussions and the decisions referred as above we are of the opinion that there is no merit in this Rule.

In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The order of stay as granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

End.

lawyer:
Alauddin Ahmed with Bhabesh Chand Sarker and Sikder Rafi Ahmed, Advocates—Fort the Appellant. 
Md Muzaffar Hossain, Advocate—For the Respondents.
parties:
Kanchan Bala Rani ----- Appellant
vs
Gita Rani Sarker and another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J : This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree, dated 10-3-1992, passed by the learned District Judge, Bogra, in LAD Case No.1 of 1989 granting letter of Administration.

2. The short facts, for the disposal of the appeal, are that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 filed Miscellaneous Case No.105, 1985 (LAD) before the District Judge, Bogra for getting letter of administration. As there was contention so the same was presented before the learned District Judge, Bogra wherein the case was registered as LAD Case No. 1 of 1989. It was the case of the respondents that on 24th Jaistha, 1384 BS. Sree Kartick Chandra Sarker executed a Will in favour of respondents. Kartick Chandra died at his residence at village Kayerpara so they were entitled to get the entire property left by Kartick Chandra on the basis of the said Will. That will was the last Will of Kartick, who voluntarily executed the same. These respondents have been possessing the scheduled property. The testator acquired 1/3rd share of the property left by Sree Godadher, the recorded tenant of CS Khatian Nos. 41, 64, 42, 38 and 59. The said properties are the subject matter of the Will. The respondents had not filed any application earlier of probate or Letter of Administration for the scheduled property in any Court. The names of Kanchan Bala Rani, Krishna Bala and Khirod Bala have been mentioned in the application as relatives of testator.

3. The daughters of the testator namely Kanchan Bala, Krishna Bala and Khirod Bala, filed written objection contending that the Will as produced by the petitioner was forged one. The scheduled property originally belonged to Godadhar who died leaving only son Gobinda, Kartick, Khagen and Jogendra are the sons of Gobinda. Kartick died leaving 3 daughters namely Kanchanbala, Krishna Bala and Khirodabala who have sons. They inherited the property left by Kartick. The wives of two brothers of Kartick creating the instant fictitious will have claimed the scheduled property. Earlier Khagen and Jogendra, two brothers of Kartick creating another Will, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 91 of 1984 (LAD) in the Court of Subordinate judge for probate which was withdrawn on 19-1-85. The Will has been created only to deprive the legal heirs of deceased Kartick Chandra. So, the case is liable to be dismissed.

4. The learned District judge by the impugned judgment and order dated 10-3-1992 allowed the case ex parte. Then Kanchan Bala, one of the daughters of Kartick, preferred this appeal.

5. Mr Alauddin Ahmed, along with Bhabesh Chandra Sarker and Mr Sikder Rafi Ahmed, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that the learned District Judge has committed an error of law in allowing the case ex parte, inasmuch as this appellant filed written objection and cross examined the witnesses of the respondents. So, the learned District Judge ought to have passed the judgment on merit considering the evidence on record. He further submits that the Will is a forged and suspicious one. The execution and attestation of the same has not been proved. He further submits that although Kartick was bound to maintain his minor daughter as per provisions of Hindu law and under section 391 of the Succession Act but he did not say anything regarding her maintenance which has made the Will unfair and inequitable.

6. Mr Muzaffar Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that appellant was negligent in conducting the case. They took several adjournments but finally did not turn up. Considering their conduct, the learned District Judge rightly allowed the case. He further submits that after about 24 years any attempt of opening the matter again, on remanding the case, would be prejudicial for the respondents. He relied upon the cases of Golam Rahman vs Hazera Khatun reported in 47 DLR (AD) 108. Md Fashuddin Mondal vs Khejnatullah reported in 1996 BLD 393 and Additional Deputy Commissioner vs Tafunnessa reported in 41 DLR (AD) 124.

7. It appears from the order sheet that 3 PWs were examined but the appellant failed to cross-examine them. On 9-3-1991 the opposite party appellant appeared and filed application for re-calling the witnesses for cross-examination which was allowed on 10-4-1991. On 15-8-1991 they cross-examination the PWs 1 and 2. On 6-11-1991, the applicant respondents filed an application to exonerate them to produce any witness and from cross- examination of PW 3 but no order was passed on that application. It further appears from the order dated 11-2-1992 that an application was filed by this appellant and the Court fixed the matter on 10-3-1992 for order. On that day, this appellant failed to appear and the Court allowed the case ex parte. In the ex parte order the learned District Judge observed as under.

“এখন সময় বেলা ১.২৫ মিনিট দাখিলকৃত উইল ও স্বাক্ষীগণের জবানবন্দী ও জেরা পাঠ করিয়া উইলটি সত্য ও সঠিক বলিয়া প্রমাণিত হয়। অতএব অত্র মামলাটি একতরফা সূত্রে বিনা খরচায় ডিক্রী হয়।”

8. In order to get Letter of Administration the propounder has to prove due execution and attestation of the Will. The onus of due execution and attestation by positive evidence lies upon the applicants because they prayed for Letter of Administration setting up the Will. Due execution means that the same was executed by the testator with knowledge and approval of the contents of the Will and he was free and capable. It requires due compliance of the provision of section 63 of the Succession Act and sections 68, 69 and 71 of the Evidence Act. Question is, whether the testator was having disposing state of mind at the time of execution of the Will and whether it was the free will and whether the testator voluntary executed the document or not. In this case it is in evidence that the testator died within 6 months from the date of alleged execution of the will. There is no evidence and finding of the learned District Judge as to the physical and mental fitness of the restator and the Will was spontaneous. It appears from the contents of the Will that he executed the Will for his entire property and has deprived his daughters, particularly the minor daughter. Earlier, the testator allegedly executed another Will in favour of his two brothers which has been stated in the Will in respect of his entire property keeping nothing for his daughters and other relatives. From aforesaid circumstances, it is difficult to hold that the same was natural, fair and equitable one. As it does not look fair so, it was duty of the propounder to explain satisfactorily as to why the testator has deprived the legal heirs from his property. The respondents, who are the beneficiary of the Will, in their evidence failed to establish any extraordinary circumstances to justify the exclusion of the heirs of deceased testator Kartick Chandra. The second Will was not free from all suspicion. So, it was the thirty of the propounder to remove such suspicion by adducing cogent evidence giving satisfactory explanation but from evidence it appears that they did not take any step to remove so. The propounders were bound to prove their case to the satisfaction of the Court and their burden was not lightened because the other side was absent. Similarly, conscience of the Court is paramount in the matter of testamentary succession. It is not denied that the husbands of the applicants did not file case No. 91 of 1984 (LAD) for probate. The same was filed after 7 years of the death of the testator. Khagendra Nath Sarker, attesting witness of this Will and husband of Gita Rani, the applicant respondent No.1 was one of the applicants of the said case. Knowing fully well about second Will he brought said Probate case. That case was withdrawn. Thereafter, wives Khogen and Jogen have filed this case. Which has also created a suspicion. From the application for letter of administration and evidence of PW 1 it appears that PW 1 has given contradictory statements regarding the date of the death of the testator. In cross she said that scribe Anil is a resident of village Shokhapukur but from the evidence of Anil (PW 2) it appears he is a resident of village Mohishpal. Attesting witness Khogendra has not been examined. Scribe PW 2 and attesting witness PW 3 have not said anything regarding time, place and manner of execution of the Will. PW 2 in cross said “আমি দলিল লিখি না। এই উইল আমি লিখিয়াছি।” Even he did not say that he read out the contents of the Will to the testator before such execution PW 3 simply said, “এই উইল নিদর্শন ১ কার্তিক চন্দ্র সরকার সম্পাদন করেন। এই উইলে আমি সই করি নিদর্শন ১/২।” He did not say that he has been executant to sign the Will. There is nothing in evidence that the execution was effected by the testator with knowledge and approval of the contents of the Will. None of the witnesses deposed as to when the talk about the execution of Will was held. Section 63 clause (c) provides that the Will shall be attested by two or more witnesses, each of whom has seen the testator sign or affix his mark to the Will or has seen some other persons sign the Will, in the presence and by the direction of the testator, or has received from the testator a personal acknowledgment of his signature mark, or of the signature of such other person; and each of the witnesses shall sign the Will in the presence of the testator, but it shall not be necessary that more than one witness be present at the same time, and no particular form of attestation shall be necessary. Where the evidence of witness did not reveal that both the attesting witnesses had signed the Will after the testator signed it, the Will cannot be said to have been proved. The petitioner filed application for exemption from production of PW 3 and his cross examination which was not disposed of. In view of circumstances, it is difficult to accept the evidence of PW 3. There is nothing in the evidence regarding the permanent place of abode of the testator.

9. In the case of Sridevi vs Joyaraja reported in AIR 2005 SC 780 it has been observed by Supreme Court of India that the propounder of the Will has to show that the Will was signed by the testator; that he was at the relevant time in sound disposing state of mind; that he understood the nature and effect of dispositions and had put his signatures to the testament of his own free will and that he had signed it in the presence of the two witnesses who attested in his presence and in presence of each other. In the case of Kashibai vs Parwatirai reported in (1995) 6 SCC 213 it has been observed by the Indian Supreme Court that "attestation" and "execution" are two different acts, one following the other. There can be no valid execution of a document which under the law as required to be attested without the proof of its due attestation and if due attestation is also not proved; the fact of execution is of no avail. Having regard to the evidence, facts and circumstances of case and decision cited above we are of the view that the execution of the alleged Will has not been proved in accordance with law as required under section 68 of the Evidence Act; read with section 63 of the Evidence Act.

10. Mr Alauddin relying upon the case of Bangladesh vs Abdul Wadud reported in 25 DLR (SC) 90 submits that it is true that on the date fixed the appellant was absent but it was the duty of the learned Court to see as to whether the profounder has been able to prove the requirements of due execution and attestation or not. In the cited case their Lordships observed as follows:

"On analysis of the evidence of the evidence with reference to averments made in the plaint it is evident that the plaintiff failed to prove his case in accordance with law. The plaint is not evidence for the proof of the case of the plaintiff. The absence of the defendant who asked for adjournment but refused on reasons assigned therefore cannot give occasion for the plaintiff to obtain ex parte decree without producing the relevant documents on the basis of which relief is sought for. The Court is bound to apply its mind with reference to the pleadings and satisfy itself as to what should be the proper proof for passing a decree on the basis of the averments made in the plaint. It appears to us that the Court below considered the nonflying of written statement by the defendant after obtaining several adjournments absolved the Court from the responsibility to examine the legality of the claim of the plaintiff."

11. In the case of Haines vs Hinkson reported in AIR 1946 PC 156 Lord Du Parcq while considering a Will charged with suspicion observed that the rules enjoyed a reasonable scepticism, not an obdurate persistence in disbelief. They do not demand from Judge, even in circumstances of grave suspicion a resolute and impenetrable incredulity. He is never required to close his mind to the truth.

<u>12. Considering the facts, circumstances evidence and other materials on record and decisions as referred above, we are of the view that the profounder have failed to prove the due execution and attestation of the Will and the testator had sufficient mental capacity to execute the Will and the same was executed by the testator spontaneously and was read over and explained to him before so execution.</u>

<u>13. We have gone through the decisions as cited by Muzaffar Hossain wherein their Lordships viewed against the order of remand. As we are of the view that as the propounders have failed to prove the due execution and attestation of the Will so we have no other alternative but to set aside the judgment and order as passed by the learned District judge. As the case has been disposed of ex parte from the very beginning the appellant was negligent in conducting case which allowed the Court to pass ex parte order so we consider that for the ends of justice the learned District Judge should hear the case giving opportunity to the parties to prove their respective case as it would be heard if the case is dismissed.</u>

14. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs. The judgment and order dated 10-3-1992 as passed by the learned District Judge, Bogra, is hereby set aside and the learned District Judge, Bogra, is directed to proceed with the Case allowing the parties to adduce evidence, if they are so advised. However, the observation as made in the body of this judgment will have no binding effect upon the learned District judge, at the time of disposal of the matter.

Let the LCR of the Court below be sent down at once.

End.

lawyer:
AKM Abdul Hakim, Advocate — For the Petitioner. 
Md. Saidur Rahman, Assistant Attorney-General — For the Respondents.
parties:
Mofazzal Hossain Sarker  -----  Petitioner
vs.
Bangladesh & others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Haque J: This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondent to show cause as to why the impugned order under Memo No. Projo-3/UP-42/94/196/1(3), dated 23-3-95 (Annexure-A) passed by the respondent No. 2 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that, the petitioner was elected as Chairman of Banglabazar Union Parishad under Munshiganj District in the election held on 15-1-92. During the term of his office as Chairman the petitioner worked hard and he became very popular amongst the people of the union. Due to his popularity in the locality his election and political rivals/opponents became jealous and started spreading various rumours/ remarks against him attributing bad name of the petitioner. Some of them gave open declaration that soon the petitioner will be implicated in misappropriation case. In spite of non-cooperation of his opponents the petitioner was discharging his official duties honestly and diligently. While the petitioner was discharging his public duties as Chairman he suddenly received a letter under Memo. No. Projo-3/UP-42/94/196/1(3), dated 23-3-95 under the signature of the respondent No. 2 suspending the petitioner under section 65(1) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 and directing him to hand over the charge within 3 days.

3. In the said suspension order dated 23-3-95 it has been stated that for the interest of Union Parishad it is not desirable that the petitioner should be allowed to continue as Chairman of Banglabazar Union Parishad as because of the pendency of a criminal case against him and others for misappropriation of 2007 Kgs of rice and 937.5 Kgs of wheat under sections 409/109/420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947. The petitioner contended that before issuing the aforesaid order of suspension dated 23-3-95 the respondents neither issued any show cause notice upon the petitioner nor they gave him any opportunity of being heard and/or explaining of his position.

4. The petitioner after receipt of the said order of suspension dated 23-3-95 served a notice upon the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 through his lawyer demanding justice and requested them to withdraw and/or rescind the said suspension order within 3 days. It was clearly stated in the said notice demanding justice that if the demand is not complied with within the stipulated period of 3 days time then it shall be deemed that the justice has been denied to him. The respondents did not comply with the notice demanding justice. The petitioner under such situation was compelled to move this Court under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and obtained the present Rule.

5. Mr. AKM Abdul Hakim, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the petitioner being an elected Chairman of Banglabazar Union Parishad should have given a show cause notice and/or opportunity of being heard before issuance of the impugned order of suspension dated 23-3-95. The respondents No. 2 having not issued any show cause notice and/or affording the petitioner any opportunity of being heard and/or to explain his position, the impugned order of suspension is illegal and without lawful authority. The learned Advocate further submits that the respondents have used the provision of section 65(1) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 as a cloak to victimise the petitioner inasmuch as they passed the impugned order without forming any opinion as to the correctness of the allegations and, as such, the impugned order is malafide. The learned Advocate submits that the Government having not initiated any proceeding to ascertain whether the petitioner is guilty of misconduct for anything done by him during the tenure of his office as Chairman, they acted without any lawful authority in passing the impugned order of suspension.

6. The respondents No. 1 has filed affidavit-in-opposition and denied the material allegations made in the petition. It has been stated in the affidavit-in-opposition that the Local Government Division of the Ministry of LGRD and Co-operatives had got the right to suspend any Union Parishad Chairman under section 65(1) of the Ordinance if any proceedings have been initiated for the removal of the Chairman under section 12 of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 or where any criminal proceedings under any law have been started against such Chairman. It has been further contended by the respondents No. 1 that the petitioner was put under suspension under section 65(1) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 for the greater interest of the Union Parishad.

7. Mr. Saidur Rahman, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the respondents, submits that the petitioner was suspended by an order dated 23-3-95 because criminal proceedings had already been started against the petitioner for alleged mis-appropriation of 2007 Kgs. of rice and 937. 5 Kgs. of wheat under sections 409/109/420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1974. The issuance of order of suspension under section 65 (1) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 does not contemplate any show cause notice and/or giving any opportunity to the petitioner of being heard and/or of explaining his position. Therefore, the learned Assistant Attorney-General submits that the enabling power under section 65(1) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 has been legally exercised and there is no illegality in it.

8. For the sake of convenience section 65 (1) of the Local Government (Union Parishad) Ordinance, 1983 is quoted as under:

"65. Suspension of Chairman and Member in certain circumstances—(1) Where any proceedings have been initiated for the removal of the Chairman under section 12 or where any criminal proceedings under any law have been started against such Chairman or whereon an enquiry by the Government he is found to be guilty of any misconduct within the meaning of section 12(1) and, in the opinion of the Government, the exercise of power by him as Chairman is either likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the Union Parishad or undesirable from the point of view of public interest, the Government may, by order in writing, place such Chairman under suspension; and during the period of suspension as Acting Chairman elected in accordance with the provisions of section 16 shall discharge the functions of the Chairman until the termination of the proceedings, or in the event of the Chairman being removed as a result of such proceedings, or until the suspension is withdrawn or until a new Chairman is elected for the Union Parishad."

As per the aforesaid provisions Chairman or Members may be suspended in certain circumstances and they may be summarised as under :

(i) Where any proceedings have been initiated for the removal of the Chairman under section 12 of the said Ordinance. In this case no proceedings have been initiated for removal of the petitioner.

(ii) Where any criminal proceedings under any law have been started against such Chairman. In fact, the criminal proceedings have been started against the petitioner in this case.

(iii) Where upon an enquiry by the Government, he is found to be guilty of any misconduct within the meaning of section 12(1). In fact, no enquiry has been conducted by the Government and the petitioner has not been found to be guilty of any misconduct within the meaning of section 12(1). Besides the above circumstances and conditions laid down in the said section 65(1) of the said Ordinance, the Government is required to form an opinion that the exercise of power by the petitioner as Chairman is either likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the Union Parishad or undesirable from the point of view of public interest, then the Government may, by order in writing, place such Chairman under suspension. This is a condition precedent before a Government can exercise power under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance.

9. Section 65(1) of the said Ordinance, 1983 does not expressly provide that a show cause notice and/or an opportunity of being heard should be given to the Chairman before issuing the order of suspension. Section 65(1) does not also contain any provision that a show cause notice should be given before a Government can exercise power of suspension under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance. Mr. AKM Abdul Hakim, however, submits that before a Government can exercise power of suspension under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance, it has to form an opinion on the basis of materials before it that the exercise of power by the Chairman is either likely to be prejudicial to the interest of the Union Parishad or undesirable from the point of view of public interest Secondly, the learned Advocate submits that the show cause notice should be issued before the issuance of order of suspension under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance. The fact that an elected Chairman of the Union Parishad, during the carrying out of the functions of the Chairman, it is likely that he may incur lot of displeasure from various quarters including his opponents. Therefore he must be given an opportunity of being heard before his right to hold elected office is suspended under section 65(1) of the Ordinance. In support of his arguments he has placed reliance in the decision of a case of Sk Ali Ahammad vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others reported in 40 DLR (AD) 170, wherein the statutory principles of natural justice laid down in the case of the University of Dhaka vs. Zakir Hossain and others, reported in 16 DLR (SC) 722 has been discussed.

In 16 DLR (SC) case it has been held that

"In all proceedings by whoever held, whether judicial or administrative, the principles of natural justice have to be observed if the proceedings might result in consequences affecting the person or property or other right of the parties concerned. "

It has been further held that

"This Rule applies even though there may be no positive words in the statute or legal document whereby the power is vested to take such proceedings, for, in such cases this requirement is to be implied into it as the minimum requirement of fairness."

10. Relying upon the aforesaid principles laid down in 16 DLR (SC) case the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that although there is no positive express words in the Ordinance to give an opportunity of being heard but the same shall be implied as the minimum requirement of fairness before an elected Chairman is suspended.

11. The learned Advocate has also referred to the case of Bangladesh vs. Md. Lokman Patwari and another, reported in 46 DLR (AD) 163 wherein it has been held that

"Mere existence of any of the three circumstances mentioned in the section will not be enough for taking action against the Chairman. The Government must also form an opinion in terms of the language mentioned in section 65(1). The opinion is to be formed by the Government after considering the materials before it and after being satisfied that the materials have a casual connection with the kind of opinion that it is required to form."

12. In the instant case we find that there is no materials at all on which the Government formed an opinion. All that it says is that a criminal case has been started against the petitioner and it is not desirable in the interest of the Union Parishad to allow him to continue to function as Chairman. It cannot be said from the very reading of the impugned order itself and from the materials furnished that the Government had legally formed opinion before the issuance of order of suspension.

13. The question of observance of principles of natural justice has also been considered in the aforesaid case reported in 46 DLR (AD) 163 wherein it has been observed in paragraph No. 17 that

"it was argued before the High Court Division that the impugned order was illegal because it was not preceded by a show cause notice to the writ petitioner. The High Court Division noted the argument in great detail but failed to give any decision in the matter, without telling why. While granting leave we left this question to be agitated afresh by the writ petitioner-respondent and Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed has argued the matter in detail. The learned Additional Attorney-General points out that at least in this case the plea of absence of a show cause notice is not available, because the writ petitioner was absconding. We find the submission of the learned Additional Attorney-General to be quite reasonable in the facts and circumstances of the case."

14. It is interesting to note that the learned Additional Attorney-General points out that, "at least in this case" the plea of absence of a show cause notice is not available, because the writ petitioner was absconding. Had the petitioner not been absconding as in the present case, according to the learned Additional Attorney-General, the plea of absence of show cause notice was available to him. In other words had the writ petitioner in that case not been absconding a show cause notice was necessary before issuance of the order of suspension. On the facts before it the Appellate Division has held that the submission of the learned Additional Attorney-General was quite reasonable. Admittedly in the present case the writ petitioner was not at all absconding. Therefore applying the underlying meaning of the observations made in the aforesaid case with regard to the principles of natural justice we are of the view that the Government is required to give a show cause notice before any power for suspension is exercised under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance. This is also consistent with the decision reported in 16 DLR (SC)'s case wherein it has been clearly held that the principles of natural justice applies even though there may be no positive words in the statute or legal documents whereby the power is vested to take such proceedings, for, in such cases this requirement is to be implied into it as the minimum requirement of fairness. The office of Chairman is a public representative office and its deprivation, however temporarily, will be strictly viewed with.

15. It has been stated in the impugned order dated 23-3-95 that the writ petitioner did not distribute 2007 Kgs. of rice and 937.5 Kgs. of wheat to the VGD Card holders and he created forged and fake master-roll. It has been further stated that the allegations have been proved and consequently a Criminal case under sections 409/109/420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 has been started against the writ petitioner but it does not say how the allegations have been proved. There are no materials on record to form such opinion. Moreover, the Government has issued the impugned order of suspension on the ground that the petitioner chairman Md. Mofazzal Hossain Sarker is involved in the case of misappropriation and the same is pending against him. Therefore, it is not desirable that he should be allowed to continue to function as Chairman of Union Parishad because that would be against the interest of the administration.

16. Be that as it may unless, the criminal case that has been started against the petitioner has been terminated either this way or that way it is not understood how the Government has alleged in the order of suspension that the allegations have been proved. The Government has prejudged the entire criminal case even without giving the delinquent Chairman an opportunity of being heard and explaining his position with regard to the alleged non-distribution of 2007 Kgs. of rice and 937. 5 Kgs. of wheat. Element of prejudging the case is an indication of malafide inas much as before the allegations have been proved in a court of competent jurisdiction the Government cannot say that the allegations have been proved and it is necessary that the power under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance should be exercised. Before the Government had formed an opinion to exercise power under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance the minimum requirement of fairness, i.e. principles of natural justice ought to have been complied with. The omnibus statement that the allegations of misappropriation have been proved cannot be a basis to exercise power under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance. There is no iota of evidence on record to support that the Government had formed opinion before exercising power under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance. In the case of Bangladesh vs. Md. Lokman Patwari and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) 163 the Appellate Division has observed that, "The office of Chairman is the public representative office and its deprivation, however temporary, will be strictly viewed at". The petitioner should be given an opportunity to explain with regard to the allegation made against him. It has also been held in the said case reported in 46 DLR (AD) 163 that mere existence of any of the three circumstances mentioned in the section will not be enough for taking action against the Chairman. The Government must also form an opinion in terms of the language of the section We do not find any materials whatsoever of record as to how the Government had formed its opinion in exercising the power of suspension as provided under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance. Mere filing of a criminal case against the Union Parishad Chairman cannot by itself be the sufficient materials to form an opinion by the Government to suspend the elected Chairman from performing his duties and functions as Chairman. In fact, the Government had no materials except the said criminal case before forming the opinion to suspend the Chairman.

17. In that view of the matter we hold that the impugned order of suspension cannot continue. Moreover, the petitioner is on bail and no proceedings to remove him from the office of the Chairmanship has yet been started. But he has been put under suspension and depriving him from opportunity of performing his duties and functions of the elected office. Impugned order of suspension was not preceded with show cause notice and is therefore bad in law.

<u>18. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the law points involved we hold that before a Government can exercise power of suspension under section 65(1) of the Ordinance, 1983 the delinquent Chairman should be given an opportunity of being heard as well as the Government must form an opinion on the basis of the materials before it that the suspension order is necessary in the interest of the Union Parishad or undesirable from the point of view of public interest. In the instant case neither of the conditions as contemplated under section 65(1) of the said Ordinance, 1983 has been complied with and thereby we find that the impugned order of suspension has been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.</u>

19. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order No. Projo 2/UP-42/94/196/1(3), dated 23-3-95 is declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

It is hereby directed that the petitioner shall be allowed to resume his function as Chairman pending hearing of the said criminal case and/or till the expiry of term of his office whichever is earlier.

End.
