full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J : This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 7-3-1993 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, now Joint District Judge, 3rd Court Dhaka in Title Suit No. 211 of 1983. By the said decree the trial court dismissed the suit, therefore, the plaintiffs as appellants preferred the instant appeal.

2. The plaintiffs brought the suit stating inter alia that the suit land described in schedule A of the plaint originally belonged to Rajendra Narayan Nondi in 16 annas share with possession, accordingly, CS khatian was prepared in his favour, thereafter one Akhil. Chandra Dhar raised claim over the said land, therefore, litigation cropped up in between the heirs of Rajendra Nondi in one side and said Akhil Chandra Dhar on the other and at one stage the widow of Rajendra Narayan Nondi, namely, Sreemati Promoda Sundori Daishya, having been appointed as guardian of her two minor sons Norendra Nondi and Khagendra Narayan Nondi, admitted that said Akhil Chandra Dhar was the owner of the property described in schedule A to the plaint, therefore, she executed a Nadabi Nama in favour of Akhil Chandra Dhar on 22-7-1924 and got it registered; thereafter Okil Chandra Dhar being the owner in possession of schedule A property sold the same in favour of Jotindra Mohan Chattaijhee and Sheta Nath Banerjhee by a registered kabala dated 28-7-1925; the said Jotindra Nath Chatterjhee and Shetta Nath Banerjhee as purchasers having been in possession of the schedule A property got the same partitioned amicably whereupon Sheta Nath Banarjhee got a sham of 1 Bigha 19 Khatas and 15.48 chattak and the remaining area fell in the sham of Jotindra Mohan; Jotindra Mohan got the B schedule property in his exclusive possession, upon amicable partition with Sheta Nath Banarjhee and while he was in possession entered into an agreement for sale thereof on 16-1-1994 in favour of Bama Charan Paul; Bolo Ram Paul, Horo Lal Paul and Gopal Paul, thereafter, by a registered Kabala dated 25-7-44 transferred the schedule B property in favour of the said Bama Charan Paul, and his three brothers handed over possession; thereafter Bama Charan Paul and the others sold the B schedule property to Hafizuddin the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 1-10, Taheruddin the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 11-16 and Hajee Afseruddin the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 17-26 by a registered kabala dated 16-8-52; after purchase of B schedule property, the predecessors of the plaintiffs applied for permission from the DIT on 11-1-64 for the construction of three-storied pucca building over the suit plot No. 76 and when construction of the said building was almost over, at that stage on 30-3-66 they received a notice from the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to the effect that government has acquired suit plot No.76 along with other land for the construction of North South Road there-after the- predecessor of the plaintiffs challenged the said notice in Writ Petition No. 265 of 1966 where DIT also contested and ultimately DIT abandoned the plan of acquisition of the said land; thereafter the predecessor of the plaintiff constructed shops and garage over the B schedule land and then let it out to different tenants; the SA Khatian was wrongly prepared in favour of the defendants thereafter the RS record was correctly prepared in favour of the plaintiffs; further case of the plaintiffs is that though Rajendra Nondi had no son in the name of Dezenda Narayan, yet the defendants created a deed purported to have been executed by Dezendra Narayan in favour of the defendants; the plaintiffs also came to know in recent time that one imposter claiming himself as Dezendra Narayan Nondi, instituted Title Suit No. 25 of 1975 impleading one Aferuddin contractor and Afiluddin contractor as defendants before the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and upon practising fraud upon the court obtained an ex parte decree dated 23-8-76 in the said suit; it was also detected by the plaintiffs that the defendant No. 33, Bashir Miah in collusion with defendant Nos. 25-27 instituted Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka where he also obtained a decree on 6-4-78 in the said Title Suit No.50 of 1978 on the basis of an alleged amalnama executed by Bama Charan Paul and his brothers in favour of said Bashir Miah and on the basis of the alleged rent receipt in connection therewith and on the basis of those papers created by the defendant No. 33, they are trying to enter into possession of the schedule B land. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that the defendants also approached the Martial Law authority for taking over possession in the suit schedule B land, it is also the case of the plaintiffs that the predecessors of the plaintiffs instituted. Title Suit No. 29 of 1979 before the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in respect of the suit land but the same was dismissed for default; but the said order of dismissal took place beyond the knowledge of the plaintiffs under the circumstances as aforesaid the plaintiffs brought the suit for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 25 of 1975 was collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs.

3. The defendant No. 33 Bashir Miah, having entered appearance contested the suit upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia and Bama Charan Paul and his three brothers having been in possession of the suit land settled an area of 2.08 acres of land in favour of the defendants upon obtaining salami from them fixing annual rent, by way of a korfa settlement, thereafter upon request from the defendant No. 33, Bama Charan Paul and his three brothers granted amalnama in favour of the defendant No. 33 in respect of an area of 2.08 acres out of the said CS Khatian on 6-9-46 and possession was accordingly handed over there-after the answering defendant carried on possession over the same upon payment of rent to the Zaminders obtaining receipt and he has been in possession of his purchased land upon growing paddy and enjoying usufructs there-from ever since 6-9-46, the date on which the amalnama was executed in his favour by Bama Charan and his three brothers; the defendant. No. 33 also claimed title by adverse possession owing to peaceful possession over the same for more than the statutory period. It is also the case of the defendant No. 33 that the said 2.08 acres of land was wrongly recorded in SA Khatian in favour of late Zamir Bepari son of the Afiluddin, Khaleque Bepari son of Kadom Bepari and the Collector of Dhaka, therefore, the defendant No. 33 brought Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 impleading those persons as defendants for correction of record of rights in respect of said 2.08 acres of land and eventually got a decree in his favour in the suit on 24-3-78; thereafter on the basis of the said decree in Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 the defendant No.33 prayed for correction of record of rights in respect of the SA khatian whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1981 was registered before the ADC (Rev) Dhaka and in that proceedings the ADC having considered the materials on record including the investigation reported submitted before him, passed an order dated 23-9-81 to get the record of right corrected in favour of defendant No. 33, on the basis whereof the record of right i.e. SA khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant No. 33, as such, he has been in possession of the suit land upon payment of rent to the government. It is also the case of the defendant that the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land, therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

4. Eventually, three issues were framed by the learned Subordinate Judge, examined one witness from each side and upon conclusion of the trial dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 7-8-93.

5. Thereafter the plaintiffs as appellants preferred the instant appeal.

6. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Mizanur Rahman, Advocate for the appellants submits that the suit as framed by the plaintiff appellants was a suit for declaration that the ex parte decree is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiffs, it is maintainable without a prayer for declaration of title in the suit property since the plaintiffs were not party to the said decree.

7. Elaborating his submission the learned Advocate explained further that the trial court erroneously held that the suit is not maintainable without any such prayer since the ex parte decree sought to be declared illegal where the plaintiffs are not party to the same.

8. In substantiating his submission made to that effect the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case reported in 39 DLR (AD) 46, 9 BLC 333, 46 DLR 494 and 53 DLR 452. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for appellants that the decision cited by the learned Joint District Judge reported in 39 DLR 339 is not applicable in the instant case.

9. The learned Advocate for the appellants submits further that the defendant No. 33 having admitted in his written statement to the effect that Title Suit No. 25 of 1975 at the instance of Dezendra Narayan Nondi, as plaintiff is fraudulent and illegal and inoperative as also in his deposition as DW 1 he has admitted this position, therefore, the trial court ought to have decreed the suit on the basis of admission made by the defendant No.33. In support of such contention, the learned Advocate placed reliance on the provision of section 58 of the Evidence Act and the provision of Order XII Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate submits further that even if for the argument's sake it is assumed that the suit is not maintainable without a prayer for declaration of title then also the suit should not have been dismissed as the defect which had been alleged by the trial court in its judgment is curable by way of amendment.

10. The learned Advocate  for the appellants submits further that without curing the said defect the plaintiffs can have a decree of omitted relief or the relief which had not been sought for, if from the reading of the plaint it is found that the omitted relief i.e. declaration of title has already been narrated in the plaint and the evidence adduced in support thereof. In this connection the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case reported in 22 DLR (SC) 117, 14 DLR 657 and Nazibunnessa vs Md Abdus Sobhan Mia 1995 BLD 621 =1 BLC 70.

11. The learned Advocate for the appellants submits lastly that if the secondary evidence is accepted without objection by defendant No. 33 he cannot subsequently challenge those as illegal. In support of his contention the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case reported in 44 DLR (AD) 162.

12. Mr TH Khan, the learned Advocate appearing with Mr Md Helal Uddin Mollah on behalf of respondent No.1 (defendant No. 33) submits that the plaintiffs failed to exhibit any original deed order document. They have also failed to produce any acceptable witness to prove their title and possession moreover the exhibits are photocopies of certified copy of the original and that the photocopies are so illegible which are not even readable, there was no certificate of the Advocate Commissioner who examined PW 1 on commission about the correctness of the photocopies or that he compared the photocopies with the certified copies, therefore, the learned Advocate submits that the trial Court is perfectly justified in holding that the documents produced by the plaintiffs are not acceptable for the purpose. It has also been pointed out by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 that Exhibit 6 is the basis of the plaintiffs title in the suit schedule B land but that is also a photocopy of the deed and the plaintiffs' claim that they have purchased it from Bama Charan and 3 others on 16-8-52 but as a matter of fact this deed was executed by Bama Charan Paul alone. The plaintiffs though claim that Bama Charan and his three other brothers gave power of attorney in favour of Bama Charan Paul but the power of attorney has not been produced. Exhibit 6 shows that the power of attorney was given to one Manik Chand and the signature available in Exhibit 6 does not show that Bama Charan Paul put the signatures of his three other brothers as their attorney rather it appears that all the brothers put their signature in the said document independently. It was also pointed out by Mr Khan that Exhibit 6 contains two stamps purchased from India and the same do not contain the names in whose favour those were purchased.

13. Mr Khan has also drawn our attention to the cross-examination portion of PW 1 which reads as under:

“ইহা সত্য নহে যে, প্রদর্শনী-৬ একটি জাল দলিল। প্রদর্শনী-৬ এর দলিল লিখক এবং সনাক্তকারী সাক্ষীগণদেরকে আমরা সাক্ষী দিতে পারিব না। কেননা তাহাতা কেহই জীবিত নাই। দলিল লিখক এবং সাক্ষীগণ যে মারা গিয়াছে তাহার প্রমাণ স্বরূপ আমার কোন সার্টিফিকেট দাখিল করিতে পারিব না।”

it is also admitted by PW 1 in his cross-examination to the effect that সামনে ফটোকপি দাখিলের সময় ফটোকপিগুলির মূল দলিলগুলি তুলনা করার জন্য কমিশনারের সামনে দেই নাই। It was also disclosed by PW 1 in his cross-examination to the effect  প্রদর্শনী-৬ এ হরলাল, গোপাল বলরাম রামচরণ পালরা ৪ জনে বিক্রি করে। বামা চরণ ১নং দাতা। এদের মধ্যে এটনী হিসাবে দলিল করে বলরাম পাল। Mr Khan pointed out that by Exhibit 7 that the photocopy of release order of Bama Charan's house situated at Shantinagar there is no mention of the said land in the plaint as well as Exhibit 7 and the dated available in Exhibit 7 date 21-6-85 yet under such circumstances PW 1 deposed that government released the land on 21-6-58.

14. Mr Khan submits lastly that the findings arrived at by the learned Subordinate Judge with respect to all the exhibits produced by the plaintiffs side namely Exhibits 1-18 are based on correct appreciation of the facts and circumstances involved in the case, therefore, the penultimate decision on the basis of such findings do not call for any interference by this Court.

15. Pointing out the findings of the trial court to the effect that the plaintiffs are not in possession of the B schedule properties as per admission of PW 15 the learned Advocate submits that the suit is not maintainable at all and in support of such contention Mr Khan placed reliance in the case of Rupe Jahan Begum vs Lutfe Ali Chowdhury reported in 2 BLC (AD) 32 Mr Khan submits that a party producing secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution of the original. Even where a document is exhibited without objection the Court is to be satisfied as to its execution. In support of his contention the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Sava Rani Clam vs Abdul Awal Mia reported in 47 DLR (AD) 45.

16. Referring to section 39 of the Specific Relief Act Mr Khan submits further that the expression instrument as available in section 39 of the Specific Relief Act does not include a decree in support of such submissions Mr Khan placed reliance in the case of Bai Harkor vs Bai Shanghar reported in 18 ILR (Bom) 375.

<u>17. We have heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the materials on record relevant for the purpose of disposal of this appeal including the impugned judgment wherefrom it transpires that the trial Court with reference to the deposition of PW 1 has arrived at a positive finding to the effect that:</u>

<u>“পি, ডব্লিউ-১ রে জেরার এই বক্তব্য অনুযায়ী পরিষ্কার যে, বিজ্ঞ কমিশনার যখন বাদীর দাখিলকৃত ফটোকপিগুলি প্রদর্শনী আকারে চিহ্নিত করেন তখন তিনি মূল কগজগুলির সহিত ফটোকপিগুলি যে মূল কগজপত্রের অবিকল ফটোকপি তাহা প্রমাণ হয় নাই।”</u>

<u>It may be pointed out in this connection that Exhibits 1-18 which are the basic documents of title in favour of the plaintiffs were exhibited through the deposition of PW 1 who was examined on commission by an Advocate Commissioner and in such view of the matter the trial Court has discarded those Exhibits 1-18 as inadmissible in evidence.</u>

<u>18. We have seen from the cross-examination portion of PW 1 where he has admitted that they brought Title Suit No.314 of 1985 impleading defendant No. 33 as defendant No. 31 and that Suit was a suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. It is also admitted by PW 1 that the land covered by schedule 'B' of the plaint is also covered by the plaint in title Suit No.314 of 1985 and in such view of the matter the trial Court arrived at a positive finding that admittedly the plaintiffs have no possession in the B schedule property of the suit. It is also found by the learned Subordinate Judge that in view of the pendency of Title Suit No.314 of 1985 which covers B schedule land of the plaint of this suit the plaintiffs cannot maintain the instant suit merely for a declaration without any consequential relief, therefore, the learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit holding that the same is not maintainable and in doing so he has relied on the decision reported in 39 DLR 339 (Md Fazlur Rahman vs Ms Bani Rahman).</u>

<u>19. Turning to the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellants to the effect that the instant suit is one covered under section 39 of the Specific Relief Act and not a suit under section 42 thereof. In support of his submission the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of Sifia Khanam Chowdhury vs Faizun Nessa Chowdhury reported in 39 DLR (AD) 46. Having gone through the said judgment it appears that the appeals before their lordships arose out of a common judgment of the High Court Division disposing of two section Appeals arising respectively from Title Suit No. 532 of 1967 and Title Suit No. 87 of 1969 in one suit a simple declaratory decree was sought to the effect that a sale deed purportedly executed by the respondent was void and in the other suit recipients of the sale deed prayed for establishment of her title on the basis of the said sale deed. The sale deed was held void all through upto the Appellate Division and in that case their lordships delivered the aforesaid judgment holding to the effect that a suit for mere declaration that an instrument was void is maintainable without a prayer for consequential relief but the facts involved in the instant suit is different mainly because the plaintiffs in the suit before us prayed for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in a previous suit is not binding upon them although admittedly the plaintiffs are not party to the said suit, therefore, in our opinion, the decision cited by the learned Advocate for the appellants is not applicable in the instant suit before us.</u>

<u>20. Having gone through the other decisions namely, the case of Abdul Kashem Howlader vs Sultan Ahmed reported in 9 BLC 333. In support of his submission that the instant suit is not under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act but a suit under section 39 thereof and that the plaintiffs can maintain the suit for mere declaration without any consequential reliefs. Having gone through the said judgment we find that the same is also not applicable in the instant suit simply because of the fact that the plaintiffs are found not to be in possession of the suit land rather as per admission of PW 1 they are out of possession of the suit land but in that suit as cited by the learned Advocate the plaintiffs being over owner in possession of the suit brought the suit for mere declaration without any consequential relief.</u>

<u>21. Turning to the case of Moulavi Abdul Mannan vs Md Rafiqul Islam reported in 46 DLR 439 we find that it was a case of a Nikah registrar who was appointed under section 5(1) of the said Rules on temporary basis until a Nikah Registrar was licensed on regular basis, obtained a decree in his favour with permanent injunction but subsequently the plaintiffs was appointed as a permanent Nikah Registrar and he was not a party to the earlier suit yet it was held that he can maintain the suit subsequently for a declaration that the decree in earlier suit was not binding upon him but the fact in the instant case in completely different more particularly when admittedly the plaintiffs is not in possession of the suit land but in that case permanent Nikah Registrar was very much in the office and admittedly he was holding the office of Nikah Registrar on a regular basis.</u>

22. We have also gone through the other decisions referred to by the learned Advocate for the appellants but going through the contents thereof we find that each of those decision are dissemble from those of the facts involved in the instant suit, therefore, we do not find any of those decisions has any applicability in the instant appeal.

<u>23. Turning to the decision cited by the learned advocate for the respondent No. 1 we do not feel it necessary to enter into the question of law raised by the learned Advocate on his behalf referring to the decisions as aforesaid but at the same time we find that the basic documents namely Exhibits 1-18 produced by the plaintiffs are indeed not admissible in evidence because those are produced as secondary evidence and admittedly those were not compared with the original thereof and this position has clearly been admitted in cross-examination by PW 1 himself. In this connection section 63(3) of the Evidence Act may be referred to and in this connection it may be pointed out that a party producing secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution of the original even where a document is exhibited without objection the Court is to be satisfied as to its execution, therefore, in our opinion, the plaintiffs utterly failed to prove the case before the trial Court as such it has rightly been dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge now Joint District Judge.</u>

<u>24. We are also in complete agreement with the learned Subordinate Judge to the effect that the suit is not maintainable in its present form as it has been brought for mere declaration to the effect that ex parte decree passed in a suit earlier is not binding upon him without seeking and other relief more particularly when we have also noticed the PW 1 had admitted that he is not in possession for the suit land more particularly in view of his admission to the effect that a suit brought by them earlier in respect of the self-same land was a suit for declaration of their title and for recovery of khas possession.</u>

In view what has been stated above, this appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.
